ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ada Lovelace

code.originalText: Six-week review: bleeding and pain after palliative pelvic radiation, the first cycle of chemotherapy with pembrolizumab, blood counts, mood and opioid safety

text.paragraph: Six-week review: bleeding and pain after palliative pelvic radiation, two weeks after the first cycle of chemotherapy with pembrolizumab. [S]

Mrs. Lovelace returns four weeks after the consultation. The lung biopsy three weeks ago confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma matching the cervical tumor. She completed five days of pelvic radiation, and the bleeding stopped within a week. She had the first cycle of carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab two weeks ago, with nausea for two days. The constipation that brought her in a week ago settled within two days of the extra laxatives. Her average pelvic pain is 3 of 10 on long-acting morphine 15 mg twice a day, with a breakthrough dose on some days, and she is clear-headed in the mornings and working again. She feels low at times and finds it hard to sleep the night before treatment. She has no rash, diarrhea, or cough. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-07-14; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Alert, not sedated; blood pressure 110/70, pulse 84, weight 53.4 kg

Bleeding between periods and after intercourse, with heavier periods, a watery blood-stained discharge and a constant pelvic ache, for about five months; average pain 7 of 10 despite her opium tincture; a friable cervical mass found on examination and biopsied; cause not yet established at intake
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented final illness; superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 74 fL, ferritin 5 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding anchored to her documented final illness.

Adenocarcinoma of the endocervix, usual (HPV-associated) type, HPV 18 positive, FIGO 2018 stage IVB: a 5.2 cm tumor with left parametrial invasion, metastases to left pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes, and bilateral lung metastases on MRI and PET-CT; PD-L1 combined positive score 5, mismatch repair proficient, HER2 1+; treated with palliative pelvic radiation for bleeding and carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab, with specialist palliative care from diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit, anchored to her documented uterine cancer; the cervical site is a synthetic choice.
Cancer-related pelvic pain, nociceptive and visceral, from the cervical tumor and its left parametrial extension
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit.

Long-term prescribed opioid therapy: opium tincture for recurrent pelvic and abdominal pain for about two years, measured at times with a household spoon, converted at intake to measured oral morphine; no opioid use disorder on a DSM-5 assessment; naloxone supplied
S — Synthetic modern history anchored to her documented laudanum and opium; not a claim about her real dosing.

Drug-induced constipation from long-acting morphine and ondansetron, a week after the first chemotherapy cycle: no bowel movement for five days, with bloating and cramping but passing wind, without vomiting; no bowel obstruction on examination; potassium and calcium normal; resolved with laxatives
S — Synthetic adverse drug effect; not a historical claim.

Metastatic cervical adenocarcinoma, on first-line chemotherapy with pembrolizumab (C53.0). Stage IVB confirmed by the lung biopsy. Radiation has stopped the bleeding. Tolerating the first cycle: white cells 4.1, neutrophils 2.2, platelets 236, creatinine 0.70 mg/dL, ALT 22 U/L, so the second cycle can go ahead next week. No immune-related symptoms. [S]
Second cycle next week as planned.
Thyroid tests at six weeks, with the cycle 3 blood tests.
Restaging CT after four cycles.

Cancer-related pelvic pain, controlled (G89.3). Average 3 of 10 on long-acting morphine without sedation; she is working in the mornings. [S]
Continue long-acting morphine 15 mg twice a day and 5 mg as needed.

Iron deficiency anemia (D50.0). Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL and rising, with the bleeding stopped. [S]
Ferritin 6 to 8 weeks after the second infusion.

Long-term opioid therapy (Z79.891). Safe use; no sedation; the bowel regimen restored after the sick visit. [S]
Laxatives every day while she takes morphine.
